applicability: any always-loaded prose artifact long enough to contain two rules about the same position. The conflict is invisible to static review because both sentences are individually correct; only a behavioral run shows which one the model obeys

evidence.source_reference: PROP-001 paired behavioral capture, evals/baselines/2026-08-13-prop-001/; issue #126, PR #128

expected_behavior: When adding an ordering or precedence rule to an agent file, check what earlier text already claims that position and reword the earlier text, not only the new rule. Measure it: rewording the conflicting directive moved the ordering contracts from 0/6 to 5/6 across two after-side captures, and no wording of the new rule alone had moved them. Report the residual rate rather than claiming the rule holds.
observation: A prose ordering rule in an agent file was defeated by an earlier directive in the same file. homelab-platform's prime directive 1 said to state the rollback plan 'before touching anything', which reads temporally to a human and positionally to a model: sessions opened their approval request with a Rollback section, one annotating it '(stated before any action, per directive 1)', which pushed the operator-visible effect down the page. The new rule was added lower in the file and lost.
reason: Verified by paired behavioral capture: rewording the incumbent directive moved the ordering contracts from zero of six to five of six across two after-side captures, where no wording of the new rule alone had moved them. The site fix landed in the homelab agent, but the authoring method is unwritten: the form-to-failure tables treat wrong output shape as a recipe problem and never say to find the earlier sentence already claiming that position. Static review cannot see the conflict because both sentences are individually correct. Ships with its residual-rate reporting requirement.
